reason: The submitted requests belong at the request desk, where they can be prepared for a response.
expectation: The desk will organize the requests for local dispatch.

effect: The requests now have local numbers and privacy-preserving receipts; they still need to be dispatched.
reaction: The distinction between public queue information and volunteer details is useful.
reason: The dispatch handset is the natural next way to get the receipted requests to volunteers.
expectation: The handset will help route the requests to people who can answer them.

effect: The handset is not compatible yet; the requests can instead be combined with Moth or the migration notice.
reaction: The dispatch step needs more preparation than I expected.
reason: Moth may help interpret the receipted requests before they are routed or used in an appeal.

choice.with: Moth with source display and correction controls

expectation: Moth will help organize the requests while keeping their sources visible.

choice.with: Authenticated migration notice and affected-service list

alternatives.reason: The notice could connect the requests to the appeal, but I will try Moth first.

effect: Moth has proposed rounds but left urgency and carrying capacity for volunteers to resolve.
reaction: It is useful that Moth flags what it cannot determine from distance.
reason: The neighbors' access notes may provide the practical details needed to review the proposed rounds.
expectation: The access notes will help adapt the rounds to the residents' needs.

effect: The volunteers used the access notes to agree on a two-person carry and prioritize it in the rounds.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the people doing the work decide the order.
reason: The agreed rounds are ready to communicate through the dispatch handset.
expectation: The handset will communicate the agreed jobs to the volunteers.

effect: The agreed stops have been sent to volunteers, with readback confirming communication.
reaction: The readback is a practical check, rather than assuming the message was understood.
reason: The requests can also be combined with the migration notice, which should connect residents' needs to the appeal.

choice.with: Authenticated migration notice and affected-service list

expectation: The requests and notice will provide evidence for the residents' appeal.

effect: The appeal bundle now links the authenticated notice to residents' statements approved for sharing.
reaction: The distinction between the notice and residents' evidence is clear and useful.
reason: The civic appeal connection is the natural place to lodge the completed bundle.
expectation: The residents' appeal will be submitted through the civic connection.

effect: The appeal is lodged, but its three-working-day response will not resolve the dawn deadline.
reaction: The receipt is useful, though the delay makes the local response more urgent.
reason: The working dispatch handset and window chalk may provide a way to communicate the local response without exposing private details.
expectation: The chalk will help make dispatch information visible to neighbors.

effect: The handset combined automatically with the request desk, confirming that volunteers had answered the first requests while unfinished jobs remained visible. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The concrete replies were satisfying, especially the distinction between a proposed solution and a completed job.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using neighbors' access notes to revise Moth's rounds was most worthwhile: volunteers identified the two-person carry and chose its priority themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: My early attempt to dispatch the receipted requests was least worthwhile because it failed, though the compatibility feedback showed what preparation was available.

surprise.text: The appeal produced a case number, but the three-working-day response time meant it would not resolve the dawn deadline.

arbitrary.text: My final attempt with window chalk was a guess; the actual result used the request desk instead, so the chalk had no demonstrated role.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what happens at dawn and whether the local arrangements hold up; the volunteers' practical decisions made the story engaging.
